paragraphs: Rabbi Yose of Yukrat: Taanit, chapter 3, 23b–24a. Rashi explains that Yukrat is a place-name. Perhaps it is Derokart, where Rav Huna lived; see Yud Keret above. He did not spare his son or daughter. His son said: ‘Fig tree, bring forth your fruit.’ Because he troubled his Maker to bring it forth out of season, he should be gathered out of season. His daughter was beautiful; a man looked through an opening to see her. He said: ‘You cause people distress; return to your dust.’ He had a donkey: when people rented it, they placed its hire upon it; if they added or subtracted, it would not return. His student Rabbi Yose bar [Avin; patronymic missing in print] left him and went to Rav Ashi; see his entry, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa. He and his father are buried in the town of Kiyumaya under a broken dome. Every time they repair it, it breaks. The fig tree that brought forth fruit out of season still stands, with a spring of living water beside it (גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]). It seems to me he erred and thought Rabbi Yose brought forth the fruit out of season. Gilgulei Neshamot writes that he was Elisha, who set bears upon children, and now set death upon his son and daughter. They were the rectification of Amnon and Tamar, David’s children; see Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha above. They came in reincarnation as the pious man’s children for their rectification. Here matters are reversed: David never distressed one of his children by asking, ‘Why did you do this?’ while this man was cruel out of zeal for the Lord of Hosts. Under chet it writes: Rabbi Yose of Yukrat’s donkey rectified the officer who said, ‘Would God make windows in heaven?’ He intended to teach that the generation were the flood generation and deserved a flood, and the Holy One, blessed be He, does not perform a miracle for liars. He was not so entirely irreverent, but did not believe the prophet and also spoke accusations against His children. Rabbi Yose was Elisha; it is known that every woman who looked at him died immediately, and he set bears upon children. Under dalet it writes that Dinah was Rabbi Yose’s female donkey; because she attached herself to Shechem son of Chamor, she descended in this embodiment for her rectification. End quotation. See part 1, year 3043.
